findings.rule: REVIEW.md framework rule: plan.md must reflect the diff; a diff that departs from the plan without a plan.md update in the same commit is non-compliant (coding-standards rule 3: a departure updates plan.md in the same commit).
findings.summary: shell_guard is imported at module scope in tests/test_hooks.py, but plan.md's Order of work step 1 (and its Files-that-change entry for this file) requires the import be placed inside each test function specifically so a failure in the new tests cannot abort collection of the rest of the file, and plan.md was never updated in any commit on this branch to reflect that the diff does the opposite.

_absolute_rule_root has no remaining production caller after ci_settings_file was rewritten to call _posix_root(root_resolved.as_posix()) directly; only tests/test_ci.py still calls it, so it is now dead code in the shipped module.

findings.rule: coding-standards rule 7 (small functions; plugin/skills/coding-standards/check.py's LONG_FILE=500 advisory).
findings.summary: The new hook script is 985 lines, nearly double the coding-standards advisory limit of 500 lines for a single source file, with no split proposed in plan.md.

Now that FRAMEWORK_SUITE (line 32) is itself tuple(p.name for p in run.discover(FRAMEWORK_CASES)), the assertion names == list(FRAMEWORK_SUITE) compares two calls to the same discovery function against each other and is tautological, so a bug in run.discover (a skipped or duplicated case folder) would no longer be caught by this line.
